Hi Alicia — thanks for the sample, that helps. High-level answers first, then I pulled in Karthik (billing/product) for the detailed math.

Short answers:
- We bill at the request level for combined input+output tokens after tokenization. If a single API call references a 12k token retrieval + prompt + generated output, that request will be metered against the applicable bucket(s).
- We apply a 60-second billing window for streaming/interactive workloads for prefix reuse (i.e., identical KV cache reuse within the window avoids recharging full context).
- Minimum per-request charge: our standard floor is 8 token-equivalent units per API call. That floor can be adjusted via pilot concessions — more below.

I'll paste Karthik's detailed examples in a follow-up. If procurement needs language for the SOW, we can provide a short clause and a sample credit schedule.

Hi all — adding concrete rules and short worked examples so procurement can reconcile to invoices. These are our current production billing rules (TL;DR in plain English at top, then examples):

Production rules (summary):
1) Per-call metering: we bill based on the tokenized sum of user prompt + model output + any attached prefix/context that is materialized into the KV cache for the request.
2) Context fallthrough: if a call references a persisted context that exceeds the customer's committed context slab, we charge for the next higher slab for that call (there's no pro-rata within a single request). Example: committed slab 4k tokens, call uses 6.2k -> billed as 8k slab unless otherwise negotiated.
3) Billing window & reuse: identical KV cache reuse within a 60s window is free for subsequent calls (no double-charge for the same cached prefix). Different user IDs or cache keys are distinct.
4) Minimum floor: default per-request floor = 8 token units. This prevents micro-churn (e.g., heartbeat pings) from creating many tiny charges. We can offer a pilot concession of a 6-token floor for the first 90 days or a one-time overage credit — whichever aligns with the pilot structure.
5) Fractional smoothing: we round per-call token calculations to the nearest 0.1 token for accounting, but invoice grouping applies the slab/minimum rules above. Fractional smoothing is only visible in usage exports, not on invoice line items which use rounded slabs.

Worked examples (approx):
- Case A: single request with 300 token prompt + retrieval merged 5,700 tokens + expected output 200 tokens = total 6,200 tokens. If customer's committed slabs are in 4k/8k bands, we bill this call as an 8k slab. On an invoice this shows '8k token unit charge' not a 6.2k line.

- Case B: repeated small pings: 10 calls in 30s, each containing 3 tokens of variable metadata. With 60s KV reuse disabled (different keys), each call hits 8-token floor -> billed as 10 x 8 tokens. If keys are identical and KV reuse applies, only the first call triggers the floor and subsequent calls within 60s incur zero additional token charge for the cached prefix but still bill for any new user prompt/output tokens.

- Case C: streaming long output split into multiple chunks: we compute tokens across the entire logical request; if the client keeps the stream alive and the model emits 2,500 tokens over 3 minutes, that's a single request billed on the summed tokens (subject to slabs and floor). If the client reconnects as a new request, it's billed separately.

Negotiation levers for pilots / enterprise deals:
- Lower per-request floor (we can go down to 4 tokens for heavy volume pilots but require a short trial period and increased minimum commit).
- Slab mapping adjustments: map your common 6k pattern to a custom 6k slab (instead of 8k) for committed capacity agreements; this is a contract-level change and impacts pricing tiers.
- One-time usage credit: we can apply a retroactive credit for pilot months to smooth adoption risk.

I'll add a short redlined paragraph for the SOW if you want procurement language.

—Karthik

Agreed pilot concessions (90 days):
- Per-request floor reduced from 8 tokens -> 6 tokens for pilot window (first 90 days after go-live).
- One-time usage credit: Redwood will apply a $5,000 credit to cover September pilot delta (applies to invoice following activation).
- Slab mapping: we will create a custom slab mapping so the common 6.2k pattern is billed at a 6k slab for the pilot only; this will be visible on the usage export but the standard catalog will revert on contract renewal unless agreed otherwise.
